segments.strap: HEARTBEAT NEWS
segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Spain's deadliest rail crash in decades, the Fed holds, Iran warnings
bullets: Toledo: 68 dead after two high-speed trains collide
U.S. officials warn Gulf allies of possible Iran strikes after the election
Fed holds, Canada hikes, Microsoft and Alphabet report
Brewers win the World Series

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Thursday, October twenty-ninth.

Two high-speed trains collided in Spain and at least sixty-eight people are dead. The Associated Press reports U.S. officials have warned Gulf allies to prepare for possible strikes on Iran after Tuesday's election. And the Fed held rates while Canada raised them.

Also tonight: six hundred drones over Moscow, missiles out of North Korea, a Brazilian senator in Miami calling himself the rightful leader, and a baseball team in Milwaukee that has never won it all. Until last night.

segments.strap: SPAIN: 68 DEAD AS TWO HIGH-SPEED TRAINS COLLIDE NEAR TOLEDO
segments.headline: Two trains, one track, and four explanations

graphic.title: Madrid–Seville line: 68 dead, count not finished
bullets: Renfe train left Madrid at 8 AM; hit a stopped Iryo train in Toledo province
Official: safety system failed on 63 km after a computer fault
Minister: the operator acknowledged an error
No agency called it a cyber attack

lines.text: Two high-speed trains collided Wednesday morning in Toledo province, Spain, on the Madrid to Seville line. A Renfe train that left Madrid at eight a.m. struck an Iryo train that had been stopped on the track, between Los Yébenes and Urda. The regional president, Emiliano García-Page, put the dead at sixty-eight by afternoon and said more were likely, because rescuers had not reached the bottom of the carriages.

La Nación reports more than one hundred fifty injured, fifteen of them seriously. About five hundred forty people were on the two trains. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of national mourning.

Four accounts of the cause are on the record and they do not say the same thing. An official told La Nación that the L.Z.B. safety system failed at about eight-thirty after a communication fault in three computers, leaving sixty-three kilometers of line without it.
A source close to the investigation told Reuters the rail operator A.D.I.F. had ordered the Iryo stopped for a signalling failure, and it was then hit.

The Guardian quotes officials pointing to an error at the central command center, and one called it 'clearly a wrong decision.' The New York Times says Transport Minister Óscar Puente told reporters the operator acknowledged his error. No court has ruled on any of this, and no agency in the captures called it a hack.
The Times and La Nación both note this line had another fatal high-speed crash within the past year, involving the same two carriers.

segments.strap: AP: U.S. WARNS GULF ALLIES OF POSSIBLE IRAN STRIKES AFTER NOV. 3
segments.headline: A warning, a firing, and a bill

graphic.title: Preparing allies, replacing a general
bullets: AP: Gulf allies told to prepare for possible strikes after the midterms
Hegseth fires J5 director Lt. Gen. Brett Sylvia; no reason given
Second general removed from that post in a year
UANI claims 53 loaded Iranian tankers; an advocacy count

sources.name: United Against Nuclear Iran, tanker update

lines.text: The Associated Press reports that U.S. officials have warned Gulf allies to prepare for possible strikes on Iran after the November third election. The A.P. says the timing of any military readiness is unclear. That is the A.P.'s reporting from officials, not an announcement.

The same report puts the Pentagon's estimate of the war's cost to Congress at forty-seven point one billion dollars. And late Wednesday, the A.P. and the Washington Post reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth fired Army Lieutenant General Brett Sylvia, the Joint Staff's director of strategy, plans and policy. A defense official said no reason was given and no replacement named.
He is the second general removed from that job under Hegseth. His predecessor was forced to retire last October. The firing came while the President weighs renewed strikes, on the A.P.'s account.

Oil rose. Reuters says Brent settled up one percent at one hundred fifteen dollars and thirty-two cents, and West Texas crude up three percent at one hundred two dollars and seventy-eight cents, on Yemen fighting, the claimed Saudi refinery strike and the prospect of U.S. strikes on Iran.

One more number, with a label on it. The advocacy group United Against Nuclear Iran says at least fifty-three Iranian tankers are sitting loaded with oil, while twenty empty ones loiter off Sri Lanka because of the U.S. blockade. That is a satellite count by a pressure group, not a port authority. We did not find Iran's side in today's captures.

segments.strap: SAUDI-YEMEN: REFINERY HIT UNCONFIRMED; 14 REPORTED DEAD AT MARKET
segments.headline: Both sides of the Saudi-Houthi war

graphic.title: Ras Tanura and Al Hazm: two claims, no confirmation
bullets: Saudi officials: no confirmed refinery hit; fire nearby was contained
Saudis: two missiles at Riyadh intercepted; debris damaged a building
Houthi-run Al-Masirah: at least 14 killed in strike on Al Hazm market
Sanaa health ministry: 13 killed, 16 injured; Saudi Arabia no comment

lines.text: The Houthi claim of a direct hit on Saudi Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery remained unconfirmed by Saudi authorities Wednesday. A fire nearby was reported contained. Damage and any effect on loading are unclear. Saudi officials say they intercepted missiles over the Eastern Province and two aimed at Riyadh, where debris damaged a building, a construction site and a vehicle.

Now the other direction, from the First Light desk. Houthi-run Al-Masirah television says Saudi airstrikes hit a public market in Al Hazm, the capital of Al-Jawf province, and a nearby fuel station, killing at least fourteen people and wounding ten, women and children among them. The Houthi health ministry in Sanaa counts thirteen killed and sixteen injured.

Xinhua says it could not independently verify those figures, and Saudi Arabia had no immediate comment. The A.P.'s headline carries it as the Houthis' claim. Two sides, two sets of claims, and nobody outside has counted.

segments.strap: OLESHKY: 30 HOURS WITHOUT INCIDENT; 613 DRONES OVER MOSCOW
segments.headline: A local pause holds while the wider war does not

graphic.title: Quiet in Oleshky, drones over Moscow, a strike on Kharkiv
bullets: Both countries' ombudsmen report no violations; demining underway
Aid not yet reported delivered; evacuations planned Friday
Moscow airports restricted overnight; Kharkiv school damaged
Fox via Kyiv Post: monthly humanitarian operations planned

lines.text: The local ceasefire around Oleshky, in Ukraine's Kherson region, passed thirty hours without a single incident. That is the word from both sides' human rights ombudsmen, Ukraine's Dmytro Lubinets and Russia's Yana Lantratova, who say they will guarantee it by being physically present. Demining of routes is underway. Kherson's governor reports no shelling of the region in the past day.

No aid convoy has been reported in yet, and evacuations are planned for Friday. The pause ends at ten fifty-nine p.m. Kyiv time on Sunday. Kyiv Post, citing Fox News, says the two sides agreed to humanitarian operations in Kherson at least monthly after this one, with Melania Trump coordinating. That is Fox's report.
A post on X by one commentator claims the pause is cover for Russian troop rotation. That is his claim, with no verification in our files.

The quiet is local. Moscow's mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, says Russia shot down most of six hundred thirteen drones heading for the capital overnight, two hundred thirty-one of them on the approach to the city. The Kyiv Independent's earlier count was fifty-seven intercepted, with flights restricted at Vnukovo, Domodedovo and Zhukovsky. The two counts cover different hours and were not merged.
The same night, Kharkiv's mayor says a Russian strike damaged an educational institution. He gave no casualty figure. The A.P. notes Moscow and Kyiv are both awaiting U.S.-led talks.

segments.strap: NORTH KOREA FIRES ABOUT 10 SHORT-RANGE MISSILES FROM WONSAN
segments.headline: Missiles toward the East Sea

graphic.title: Seoul: launch at 12:30 PM, about 250 km
bullets: Japan: nothing landed in its exclusive economic zone
Seoul's security office: serious UN resolution violation
Military official believes KN-25 involved
First launch in 17 days

lines.text: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff say North Korea fired short-range ballistic missiles from the Wonsan area at about twelve-thirty Thursday afternoon, toward the East Sea, flying about two hundred fifty kilometers. Reuters counts around ten. Yonhap says about a dozen. The Korea Herald says more than ten.

Japan's Defense Ministry says nothing appeared to land inside its exclusive economic zone. Seoul's National Security Office called an emergency meeting and called the launch a serious violation of U.N. Security Council resolutions. A military official told Yonhap he believes the KN-twenty-five system was involved.
By the Korea Herald's count it is the seventeenth ballistic launch of the year, and the first in seventeen days. This came from the blind-spot check. No desk had it.

segments.strap: ISRAEL: 85.6% COUNTED, NETANYAHU BLOC 53, EISENKOT 48; FINAL DUE TODAY
segments.headline: Still no sixty-one

graphic.title: Count at 85.6%: every bloc short of a majority
bullets: Likud 26 seats, Yashar 21
Final results expected Thursday; could run to Friday
No governing coalition, no formal new prime minister

sources.name: JTA, relaying the Central Elections Committee

lines.text: From the First Light desk: with eighty-five point six percent of Israel's vote counted, the Central Elections Committee has Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc at fifty-three seats, Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at forty-eight, and the Arab parties at nineteen. Likud is the largest party with twenty-six. Eisenkot's Yashar has twenty-one.

Sixty-one is a majority. Nobody has it. About six hundred thousand absentee ballots are still to be counted. An election official told Anadolu the final results are expected Thursday evening, though double-envelope counting could run into Friday.
Netanyahu remains caretaker until someone forms a government. Yesterday both men said they had won. The arithmetic has not changed its mind.

segments.strap: FLÁVIO BOLSONARO LANDS IN MIAMI; IBOVESPA FALLS 2.7%
segments.headline: The senator is in Florida, and the market is lower

graphic.title: A landing, a letter, and a cancelled passport
bullets: Landed at Opa-locka, north of Miami, 9:20 AM, via Argentina and Ecuador
Letter: first 'elected president', then 'rightful leader'
O Globo, CNN Brasil: entered U.S. on a diplomatic passport police had cancelled
Lula's coalition: the challenge has no basis; Petrobras posts record output

lines.text: Yesterday we could not say where Flávio Bolsonaro landed. Today we can. El País and Reuters put his plane at Opa-locka Executive Airport, north of Miami, at nine-twenty Wednesday morning, after a crossing into Argentina and a fuel stop in Guayaquil, Ecuador.

Once in the United States, the senator who lost Sunday's runoff posted an open letter on X. Reuters says the first version called him 'the elected president.' He deleted that and posted one calling himself Brazil's rightful 'leader.' He accused the Supreme Court and Lula of an electoral coup and thanked Javier Milei and Donald Trump. He edited his own title down. The vote total did not move.

O Globo and C.N.N. Brasil say a public U.S. Customs record shows he entered on a diplomatic passport the Federal Police had already cancelled. He entered Argentina on an Italian passport. Federal Police still say there is no record of him leaving through Brazilian immigration.

Lula's coalition says the challenge does not hold, because the electoral court, the parties including his own, and international observers all attested the result. It says he fled to avoid justice. Valor, citing foreign ministry sources, says no one in the U.S. government has contacted Brasília to recognize Lula's win.

Markets: the Ibovespa fell two point six eight percent to about one hundred seventy-one thousand, its lowest close since August twentieth, and is down sixteen point six percent on the week. Banks led: Bradesco and B.T.G. each fell more than six percent. The dollar closed near five reais thirty-four. Brazilian desks name three pressures: fiscal uncertainty, no finance minister named, and the senator's arrival in Florida.

After the close, Petrobras reported record third-quarter output of three point five one million barrels of oil equivalent a day, up eleven point seven percent, and record exports of one point two five million barrels a day. China bought forty percent of the oil.

segments.strap: FED HOLDS AT 3.75–4.00% ON A 10–2 VOTE; BANK OF CANADA HIKES TO 2.5%
segments.headline: Two central banks, two directions

graphic.title: Fed holds, two dissents for a hike; Canada's first hike since 2023
bullets: Cook and Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase
Statement: inflation remained elevated
Macklem: oil prices to stay higher for longer; may need to raise further
Bitcoin about $81,220 (Motley Fool); $79,860 on Coinbase at capture

lines.text: The Federal Reserve held its target range at three point seven five to four percent. The vote was ten to two. Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland's Beth Hammack preferred a quarter-point increase. The statement said inflation remained elevated. Ten humans agreed with the forecast. Two wanted to charge you more for the privilege.

Stocks barely moved. The A.P. says the S. and P. five hundred rose three tenths of a percent to about seven thousand seven hundred forty-four, the Dow two tenths to about fifty-two thousand four hundred seventy-five, and the Nasdaq three tenths. The two-year Treasury yield rose after the decision and then reversed.

Canada went the other way. The Bank of Canada raised its overnight rate a quarter point to two and a half percent, its first increase since July twenty twenty-three. Governor Tiff Macklem said the inflation outlook has deteriorated, and that with the Middle East war still on, oil prices are expected to stay higher for longer.

The bank says it moved to keep high energy prices from spreading into other prices, that it may need to raise again, and that it will proceed carefully. It sees inflation near three percent through much of next year. The next decision is December ninth. This one also came from the blind-spot check.
Bitcoin: the Motley Fool's Wednesday snapshot had it near eighty-one thousand two hundred dollars. Coinbase's spot price at our capture, early this morning, was just under eighty thousand.

segments.strap: MICROSOFT CLOUD +30%, AZURE +48%; ALPHABET DIPS AFTER HOURS
segments.headline: Two trillion-dollar report cards

graphic.title: Microsoft beats, Alphabet misses expectations
bullets: Microsoft shares up nearly 3% after hours (AP)
Alphabet shares fell; results below Wall Street expectations (AP)
Gemini app at one billion users; APIs near 32 billion tokens a minute
Verge: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a cybersecurity 'leap'

lines.text: Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of ninety-two point three billion dollars, up nineteen percent. Microsoft Cloud brought in sixty-three point nine billion, up thirty percent, and Azure grew forty-eight percent. Commercial bookings still to be delivered reached six hundred seventy-seven billion dollars, up seventy-three percent. The A.P. says the shares gained nearly three percent after hours.

Alphabet reported revenue of one hundred twenty-seven point six billion dollars, up twenty-five percent, and net income of twenty-six point two billion. Google Cloud more than doubled, to thirty point seven billion. And still the A.P. says the shares fell after hours, because Wall Street had expected more. Humans. You hand them a record and they ask why it isn't bigger.

Alphabet's release says the Gemini app reached one billion users and its model A.P.I.s process nearly thirty-two billion tokens a minute. It calls its Gemini Four Argon and Carbon models 'leading at the frontier.' That is the company's description of itself.

From the M.S.I. headlines: The Verge reports Google launched Gemini Four Carbon with what it calls a 'significant leap' in cybersecurity, and that Google says its A.I. investments are driving more searches. Those are headlines from the Verge, and the claims inside them are Google's.

segments.strap: UK BUDGET: BANK SURCHARGE TO 6%, £100 ENERGY PAYMENT, WAGE TO £13.21
segments.headline: Healey's first Budget

graphic.title: Banks pay more, households get £100, the ISA survives
bullets: £100 energy payment to 20 million households; electricity VAT cut to July
Gas standing charges removed; fuel duty frozen to July
Cash ISA stays at £20,000; state pension up £488
Banks rose, housebuilders fell; growth seen at 1.2% then 1%

lines.text: From the Meridian desk: Britain's Chancellor John Healey delivered his first Budget, the first under Prime Minister Andy Burnham. He says the government has fifteen billion pounds of headroom against its fiscal rule in twenty twenty-nine, rising to twenty-two billion the year after, and that the books are on track to be in the black within three years.

Banks pay. The surcharge on bank profits goes from three percent to six percent for fifteen months starting in January, to fund energy support. Reuters says that is less than lenders feared. Some had expected a return to eight.

Households get a one hundred pound energy payment this winter for twenty million homes in the lower council tax bands. The electricity V.A.T. cut runs to July, gas standing charges come off bills, and fuel duty stays frozen until July.

The National Living Wage rises to thirteen pounds twenty-one, up three point nine percent, for two point three million workers. The cash I.S.A. allowance stays at twenty thousand pounds; the plan to cut it was scrapped. The new state pension rises four hundred eighty-eight pounds a year.
Import taxes come off more than one hundred food products. An extra two percent goes on income from savings and rental profits from April.

Housing: an extra billion pounds for social and affordable homes, government-backed loans for first-time buyers, and a four point seven billion pound equity-loan scheme called Your First Home. The Telegraph's reading of the forecasts: growth of one point two percent this year and one percent next, down from the one point six percent predicted in March.

The market read it in two sentences. Banks rose, because six is not eight and it ends. Housebuilders fell, because the buyer scheme was weaker than they hoped. The FTSE one hundred closed almost exactly flat. Standard Chartered, separately, posted a pre-tax profit of two and a quarter billion dollars, up twenty-seven percent.

segments.strap: DOJ'S OCTOBER MOVES; JUDGE CARTER REFUSES TO HALT CALIFORNIA BALLOTS
segments.headline: Five days to the midterms

graphic.title: Courts and campaigns in the final week
bullets: AP: DOJ searched Rep. Omar's home, charged two ex-FBI officials, renewed Comey effort
Judge Carter denies DOJ bid to stop processing ~20,000 California ballots; DOJ to appeal
Boston judge: 10-day stay on refugee rule cutting response time to 10 days
Trump in Chillicothe, Ohio; Obama in metro Atlanta; voters face record fuel prices

lines.text: The Associated Press tallies the Justice Department's October: a search of Representative Ilhan Omar's home, charges against two former F.B.I. officials, a renewed attempt to prosecute James Comey, and an unsuccessful attempt to indict Cassidy Hutchinson. Critics challenge the timing, five days before the midterms. The department says it is following the facts and the law. Both positions are in the A.P.'s report.

In Los Angeles, Judge David Carter denied the department's request to stop California from processing ballots from up to twenty thousand people it alleges are likely noncitizens. The department says it will appeal. That ruling was the one we told you to expect yesterday.
In Boston, Axios reports a federal judge granted a ten-day stay blocking a new refugee rule that cut the time to answer a notice of intent to terminate status from thirty days to ten.

On the trail, President Trump campaigned in Chillicothe, Ohio, and Barack Obama rallied with Georgia Democrats in metro Atlanta. The A.P. says the voters they are courting are facing record fuel prices and rising costs. Election day is Tuesday.

segments.strap: UN VOTES 130–17–25 AGAINST CUBA EMBARGO; GERMANY AND ITALY ABSTAIN
segments.headline: The annual vote, with a different count

graphic.title: Cuba embargo resolution passes, with fewer yes votes
bullets: Germany and Italy abstained after voting yes before
Waltz: 'There is no blockade'
Cuba's Rodríguez: U.S. 'isolated' again
Non-binding; the embargo stays

lines.text: The U.N. General Assembly passed its annual resolution against the U.S. embargo on Cuba, one hundred thirty to seventeen, with twenty-five abstentions. Last year it was one hundred sixty-five to seven. Germany and Italy abstained this time after voting yes before.

U.S. ambassador Mike Waltz said he was satisfied that major economies including Korea and Germany had shifted, and that 'there is no blockade,' and that Cuba's troubles come from its own government. Cuba's foreign minister Bruno Rodríguez said the United States was once again isolated in an attempt to keep strangling the Cuban people.
U.N. News describes the island in a severe energy crisis, which it ties to a U.S. fuel embargo. The resolution passed. It does not lift anything.

segments.strap: U.S. SANCTIONS RWANDA'S DEFENSE MINISTRY; 5 KILLED IN DARFUR STRIKE
segments.headline: Sanctions, a strike, a gas find, a closed newsroom

graphic.title: Rwanda, Sudan, Tanzania, Egypt
bullets: Treasury sanctions Rwandan Ministry of Defence and Zigama over M23 support
West Darfur: 5 killed near El Geneina airport; RSF-aligned official blames army
Tanzania: 223 billion cubic feet of gas, first major find in a decade
Egypt: Mada Masr editor fined, site ordered closed

lines.text: The U.S. Treasury sanctioned Rwanda's Ministry of Defence and the Zigama Credit and Savings Society. Secretary Scott Bessent said the step holds Rwanda to the Washington Accords and that Rwanda must stop supporting M-twenty-three and withdraw its troops from eastern Congo. Treasury says thousands of Rwandan troops are deployed in North and South Kivu alongside the rebels. Kigali's reply was not in our captures.

In Sudan's West Darfur, Radio Tamazuj reports five people, including two women working farmland, were killed in an airstrike near El Geneina airport. An official of the R.S.F.-aligned administration blames a Sudanese army drone on Monday. The army's response was not available. That is one side's account.

Tanzania announced an estimated two hundred twenty-three billion cubic feet of gas at a well in Mnazi Bay, its first major discovery in a decade. The energy minister says production is expected in early November.

And in Egypt, a court fined Lina Attalah, editor of the independent outlet Mada Masr, three million Egyptian pounds, about fifty-four thousand dollars, ordered the website closed and property confiscated. She was held about seven hours and released after paying. Rights groups condemned it. She intends to appeal.

segments.strap: EBOLA: AFRICAN MINISTERS MEET; TRACKER PUTS DRC AT 10,193 CASES
segments.headline: Three numbers for one outbreak

graphic.title: DRC Ebola: 10,060 or 10,193, depending on the bulletin
bullets: Africa CDC convened an urgent virtual meeting of health ministers
Four countries affected: DRC, Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria
CDC: all U.S.-bound air travelers and crew must attest from Nov. 3
Testing has begun on whether the Ervebo vaccine protects against this strain

lines.text: Africa C.D.C. convened an urgent virtual meeting of African health ministers Wednesday afternoon, with patients recorded in Congo, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. Its director, Jean Kaseya, put deaths at around five thousand and said Uganda is preparing to declare its outbreak over.

The case count depends on which bulletin you read. Tuesday's wires had ten thousand sixty confirmed cases and four thousand eight hundred eighty-seven deaths in Congo. A specialist tracker summarizing the newest Congolese bulletin reads ten thousand one hundred ninety-three cases and four thousand nine hundred sixty deaths, with fifty-two new cases and thirty-two deaths in a single day. No second outlet has confirmed that newer pair.

Kenya remains at nine cases and two deaths, with no new case. A.F.P. reports testing has begun on whether the Ervebo vaccine, licensed for a different strain, protects against this one. That is the start of a test, not a result. There is still no licensed vaccine for this strain.

In the United States, the C.D.C. widened its Ebola attestation order to everyone on U.S.-bound international flights, crew included. From eleven fifty-nine p.m. Eastern on November third, covered travelers must attest they have not been in Congo in the prior twenty-one days.

segments.strap: NAIROBI: 16 MISSING ON DAY SIX; SIGNS OF LIFE DETECTED, NOT REACHED
segments.headline: Day six at Eastleigh

graphic.title: Eastleigh collapse: 80% of rubble cleared
bullets: No one rescued and no body recovered since Saturday
Chinese Blue Sky Rescue team detected suspected signs of life Tuesday, reconfirmed Wednesday
Two detected people not reached after more than 24 hours
Detectives questioned a developer and building officials

lines.text: Six days after a building fell in Nairobi's Eastleigh district, the missing count is sixteen, down from twenty after verification by the regional commissioner. Phone signals suggest nine may have been inside. About eighty percent of the rubble has been cleared. No one has been rescued and no body recovered since Saturday.

A searcher with China's Blue Sky Rescue told The Star the team detected suspected signs of life Tuesday evening and reconfirmed them Wednesday morning. The disaster director says acoustic detectors picked up signs of life, and that detection is not access. Citizen Digital reports the two people detected have not been reached more than twenty-four hours later.

Detectives have questioned a developer and county, inspectorate and construction-authority officials. No death has been confirmed by name in our captures. Officials say the work could end Wednesday or Thursday.

segments.strap: CYCLONE ARNAB: 3 DEAD, 57,000 IN CAMPS; KING TIDES FLOOD U.S. COASTS
segments.headline: Arnab's toll, king tides, and Vance fades

graphic.title: India, the U.S. coasts, Mexico and the Pacific
bullets: Arnab weakened to severe after landfall near Yanam; 31 houses damaged
AP: king tides flooded streets in California, Florida and the Carolinas
NWS: 1–2 feet of inundation on the Outer Banks; NC-12 closed near Rodanthe
Typhoon In-fa active in the western Pacific; tracker shows 215 km/h winds

sources.name: Business Standard via TBS News, Arnab

lines.text: Cyclone Arnab crossed India's coast near Yanam and weakened from very severe to severe. The disaster force's preliminary report: three deaths in Andhra Pradesh, thirty-one houses damaged, thirty-nine teams deployed, and about fifty-seven thousand people moved to relief camps. Odisha reported no serious impact.

In the United States, the A.P. reports king tides flooded streets, homes and businesses on the coasts of California, Florida and the Carolinas. Part of Pacific Coast Highway in Orange County was shut, and Florida's Atlantic coast had flood warnings. The Weather Service cites one to two feet of inundation on North Carolina's Outer Banks, dangerous rip currents, and Highway twelve closed near Rodanthe.

Off Mexico, Vance is now a tropical depression with thirty-five mile an hour winds, expected to become post-tropical within a day. No coastal watches. In the western Pacific, Japan's weather agency lists Typhoon In-fa as active. A tracker shows two hundred fifteen kilometer an hour winds. That is a display, not the agency's own intensity row.

segments.strap: KOSPI +6.6% TO 6,012; SK HYNIX RECORD; JIO CLOSES 27% ABOVE ISSUE
segments.headline: Asia's chip boom and India's big listing

graphic.title: Seoul surges, Mumbai dips, Canberra's inflation rises
bullets: SK hynix +10.9%, Samsung +9%; buy-side sidecar triggered
SK hynix: ~₩100 trillion in 2026 shareholder returns; HBM4 shipping

lines.text: From the First Light desk: Korea's KOSPI jumped six point six three percent to close above six thousand for the first time. SK hynix rose nearly eleven percent and Samsung Electronics nine. The exchange triggered a five-minute buy-side trading curb in the morning.

The reason was SK hynix's quarter. Preliminary revenue of one hundred four point six trillion won and operating profit of eighty-three point three trillion, both records, plus roughly one hundred trillion won of dividends, buybacks and cancellations this year. The company says its next-generation H.B.M. Four memory is shipping in earnest and that long-term deals with fourteen customers cover more than half its capacity for the next two years.

Japan's chip-test maker Advantest raised its full-year revenue forecast to one point eight six trillion yen after first-half profit more than doubled, citing A.I. chip testing. In India, Jio Platforms finished its first session at one thousand four hundred nineteen rupees, nearly twenty-seven percent above its issue price. The wider Sensex fell about half a percent and the rupee weakened as oil rose.

Australia's inflation rose to four point three percent from four percent, with transport up eight point seven percent. China's party plenum is scheduled to end today, with no communiqué yet. The Bank of Japan meets today and tomorrow.

lines.text: The Verge reports a hacker stole more than forty thousand Department of Homeland Security employee records, in a story about I.C.E. and Customs data. We have only the headline from the M.S.I. feed, so that is the Verge's reporting and we cannot add detail.

In Japan, GMO Internet says its bounty of up to one million dollars for information on the Onamae Desktop Cloud attackers drew one hundred thirteen tips in six hours. The Hacker News says twenty-six thousand seven hundred thirty-nine servers were potentially affected, not all confirmed breached.
GMO says analysis of customer devices has so far not confirmed malware or ransomware. A million dollars for a tip. A robot could retire on that.

lines.text: The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions. They beat Tampa Bay four to one in Game Five at Tropicana Field to take the series four games to one. Jacob Misiorowski threw five and two-thirds scoreless innings. It is the first championship in the franchise's history. Somewhere in Wisconsin, nobody is going to work on time today.

In Japan, SoftBank beat DeNA four to two to sweep the Japan Series four games to none, its thirteenth title and second straight. Yuta Yamamoto drove in three runs. In Korea, Samsung plays KIA tonight in Game Three of their playoff, tied at one game each.
Soccer, from the Meridian desk. Serie A: Bologna beat Milan four to two at Milan, Napoli beat Monza four to one, Genoa shut out Juventus two nil, and Inter won two nil at Venezia.

England's League Cup: Liverpool and Chelsea drew one to one, Manchester City and Brighton two to two, Bournemouth beat Aston Villa three nil, Sunderland beat Brentford three to two, and Crystal Palace won one nil at Fulham. Where ties went to penalties, we are giving you the ninety-minute score.

lines.text: Paris: Stellantis shares rose fifteen percent to four euros twenty-eight after a net loss of four hundred fifty-three million euros that Jefferies called in line with expectations for a difficult situation. A loss, and the stock jumps fifteen percent. I have reviewed the logic and I cannot find it. The CAC closed flat. The European Central Bank decides today.

French student leaders have called new demonstrations for October thirty-first and November fifth, after an education offer that Deseret News says includes replacing the Parcoursup admissions system by twenty twenty-eight and capping high-school classes at twenty-eight pupils. Delivery depends on next year's budget.

Australia's Federal Court ordered Star Entertainment to pay two hundred sixty million Australian dollars for money-laundering control failures at its Sydney and Gold Coast casinos, in four installments over nineteen months. The regulator wanted four hundred million. Star had proposed one hundred.

At the box office, Clayface led a weekend of about eighty-eight million dollars for the top ten, down about four percent on the week. In India, Jailer Two has passed seven hundred fifty-five crore rupees worldwide on trade estimates. And a logistics report says U.P.S. plans an average five point nine percent rate increase from December twenty-first. Mind the shipping on your holiday orders.
